value: minimum audible angle 4.9 deg (mean, SD 0.3) for broadband noise at 0 deg azimuth in the single-reference paradigm
method: behavioural Go/NoGo task: owls left a waiting perch to report a change in loudspeaker position; MAA taken as the angular separation at which d' reached 1.0 (cumulative normal fitted to psychometric functions, method of constant stimuli)
conditions: 3 European barn owls aged 2 to 24 years (two hatched in 2015 at Oldenburg, one in 1993 at Munich), hand-reared from about 12 days of age and kept at about 10 to 15% below free-feeding weight, all three completed all six stimulus types; stimuli 100 ms at 40 dB SPL with +/-3 dB level roving, narrowband noise (40 Hz bandwidth) at 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 and 8000 Hz plus broadband noise (500-8000 Hz); stimulus types tested in separate sessions in a sequence randomised per owl; reference fixed at 0 deg (frontal) in this paradigm; angular separations ran from 1.5 to 27 deg but loudspeakers were 6 deg apart, so positions between loudspeakers, including the separations at the filed 4.9 deg threshold, were phantom sources made by summing localisation across two loudspeakers; owls were free-flying in an echo-reduced chamber with head orientation to 0 deg checked before each stimulus; acuity differed significantly between stimulus types (F = 39.942, p < 0.001) and individual owls did not differ significantly; the smaller multiple-reference paradigm (two owls, references at -45, 0 and +45 deg) gave larger lateral MAAs than frontal ones (reference position F = 26.829, p < 0.001), and its frontal BB MAA was 3.4 deg, smaller than the 4.9 deg filed here; the Abstract's figures (14 deg at 500 Hz, 6 deg at 8000 Hz, 4 deg for broadband) are not this paradigm's Results (13.7 +/- 3.2 at 500 Hz, 8.4 +/- 1.4 at 8000 Hz, 4.9 +/- 0.3 broadband) and the paper does not explain them; they lie between this paradigm's values and the multiple-reference frontal values (14.5, 6.6 and 3.4 deg), and the Discussion gives about 4 deg for frontal broadband and 8 deg at 8000 Hz; Table 1 per-owl values not read; sound-field calibration at the owl's head not read

value: two foveae: central fovea 217.66 um deep, temporal fovea 106.38 um deep
method: histology: paraffin sections (4 um) of a fixed eye, depth measured on the section with maximum foveal depth (Fiji)
conditions: two adult male kestrels (161.23 g and 179.56 g) from a wildlife recovery centre, euthanised on veterinary grounds after severe traumatic injury (collisions with power lines and other causes incompatible with release), none euthanised for the study; left eyes used for histology; the foveal depths are single representative values from one eye (which bird not stated), with no variance or replicate; tissue fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 h, dehydrated in ethanol, cleared in xylene and paraffin-embedded, with no shrinkage correction or discussion of shrinkage; the central fovea is described as deep convexiclivate within the area centralis and the temporal fovea as a deep pit with steep walls (foveal widths 393.08 um and 265.95 um); S- and L/M-opsin immunoreactivity was found in both foveae and rhodopsin immunoreactivity was absent from the pit of both foveae (Results; the Abstract names the central pit); the authors describe the study as descriptive, with no inferential statistics; the temporal fovea is called shallow in earlier papers cited on main, here it is about half the depth of the central one

value: nine EAG-active compounds, all cuticular hydrocarbons, found by GC-EAD
method: gas chromatography with electroantennographic detection (GC-EAD) of cuticular washes; a compound counted as EAG-active if it elicited a response in at least three successful recordings
conditions: field-collected adults from two Lithuanian forests (Sept-Oct 2014-2017), held at about 4 C for 6-8 days before washing; 11 male and 12 female antennae; male washes were run on male and female antennae, female washes on male antennae only (female wash on female antennae not run); male antennae responded to all nine male-wash compounds and female antennae to four of them (Z9-23Hy, Z9-25Hy, Z6E9-25Hy, 27Hy); washes from groups of 30 insects, the female washes only from females showing abdominal elevation; the Results state that male-derived washes gave nine EAG-active compounds and female-derived washes six (read from a Results fragment), so the Abstract's nine refers to one wash type; the strongest male antennal responses were to n-pentacosane and (Z)-9-pentacosene (Abstract fragment); a hexane solvent control was used in the behavioural assay (8-12 males per treatment, each male tested once; Mann-Whitney U); with female washes males spent more time in, and reached sooner, the stimulus zone, but there were no significant differences in number of visits, total distance moved or velocity; 21Hy, 23Hy, 27Hy and Z7-25Hy were not tested behaviourally; no EAG amplitudes in mV were read; enantiomers of 3-methylheneicosane described as novel olfactory and behavioural findings in insects: the (S)-enantiomer was repellent and the (R)-enantiomer excitatory to males in the bioassay

value: in a two-arm olfactometer females were attracted to the odour of males; the other three sex pairings showed no significant bias
method: two-arm olfactometer behavioural bioassay, 50 trials for each of four sex pairings of test beetle and odour-source beetle; no antennal recordings (EAG or GC-EAD) and no compound identified
conditions: adults field-collected from rotten logs and dead wood in central Japan, some newly emerged beetles kept in an outdoor cage on Ailanthus altissima logs; control arm held an empty plastic container and the side of the odour-source animal was alternated between trials; from a Results sentence (30 words), 42 of 50 females moved toward the male odour source (chi2 = 31.39, p < 0.001), and the Results state p > 0.05 for the other three combinations; all test beetles had mated at least once during preliminary observations, individuals that showed no response to the opposite sex in preliminary checks were eliminated, and some beetles were tested more than twice, so the 50 trials per pairing are not 50 independent beetles; a beetle not reaching either arm end within 10 min was scored inactive (how inactive trials entered the chi-square test was not read); airflow 0.45 m/s, odour-source container opaque, olfactometer cleaned in 75% ethanol; the chemical structure of the male-produced attractant is still unidentified; trials were not blinded as far as read
